messages:
DataCorp-ML: @support Hey, hitting a serious issue right now — our nightly embedding job started returning a ton of 429s about 20m ago. Same payload we've been running for weeks. All embeddings failing, downstream ETL backs up. Error in logs: 
`HTTP 429 - rate_limit_exceeded: quota_window=60s, burst_exceeded=true, expected_retry_after=30`
Any quick help? :rotating_light:

Ava (support): Sorry to hear that — can you paste a sample request (no keys) and the `Content-Length`/batch size you used? Also any request IDs from responses would help. We can escalate.

DataCorp-ML: Sending a redacted snippet. We send ~60k items per batch job split into N concurrent workers. Typical batch payload example:
```json
{"model":"text-embedding-3-large","input":["..."],"batch_size":512}
```
Response header example: `Retry-After: 28`, `X-Request-Id: rc-3f9a2b`
Also saw some dimension mismatch errors intermittently: `invalid_embedding_vector_dims: expected 1536 got 1024` but mostly 429s.

Ava (support): Got it — I'm escalating to infra and runtime. @jin @marco can you take a look? I attached the request id.

Jin (eng-runtime): Looking. Initial glance at traces for `rc-3f9a2b` — request fanout to embeddings backend spiked; several backends returned 429s from the rate limiter. Two things to separate: 1) upstream rate limiter (global per-customer token bucket) refusing bursts, 2) occasional malformed vectors (dim mismatch) likely from a trimming/serialization step on client side.

Marco (infra): Metrics: DataCorp-ML's token bucket shows sustained bursts of ~4x their baseline over a 3-minute window. The burst bucket had capacity but the configured burst_cap was reached and the per-second refill couldn't keep up — generated 429s. We also hit a transient queue-growth on the embedding shard pool around 19:12 UTC.

Priya (ml-support): For the dimension error — can you confirm model selection? `text-embedding-3-large` expects 1536; if you previously used `text-embedding-2` (1024) and some jobs mixed models, that would explain intermittent mismatch.

DataCorp-ML: We did a small model test last week, possible a leftover worker used the old model. But that shouldn't cause the 429 flood across all workers.

Jin (eng-runtime): Agreed. 429s are throughput-related. Short term mitigations: reduce `batch_size` from 512 -> 128, and throttle concurrency (max parallel workers) to avoid exceeding burst window. Implement client-side exponential backoff with jitter. Recommend algorithm:
```
backoff_ms = min(60000, base * 2^attempt) + rand(0, jitter)
base = 200
jitter = 100
```
Also honor `Retry-After` header from responses.

Marco (infra): We can also apply a temporary increase to DataCorp-ML's burst cap to let current in-flight jobs drain. I'll coordinate with ops; need owner approval.

Ava (support): Customer — would you like us to temporarily raise the burst cap while you roll out client changes?

DataCorp-ML: Yes please, that would help. We'll patch the client today and re-run with lower concurrency.

deploy-bot: ops-change rc=ops-871: increased burst_cap for tenant datacorp-ml from 4x to 8x for 30 minutes — change created by Marco.

Marco (infra): I triggered a 30m uplift. Watching metrics now — queue length dropped ~45% within 2 minutes and 429s subsided. There's still a small tail because of retries.

Priya (ml-support): On dimension mismatch: please run a local quick check script on a sample file to assert vector size before sending. Example Python snippet:
```python
import numpy as np
vec = np.array(get_vector())
if vec.shape[0] != 1536:
    raise ValueError('bad-dim: expected 1536')
```
Also recommend tagging model explicitly in the job definition so no worker uses an older default.

DataCorp-ML: Running client patch now — switched batch_size to 128, limited workers from 20 -> 6, added jittered backoff honoring `Retry-After`. We'll restart in 15m and report.

Ava (support): Thanks — while you do that, we'll open a ticket to add a runbook for large embedding fanouts. @jin can you capture the triage steps so we can codify?

Jin (eng-runtime): I'll draft a short playbook: detection (sudden spike in 429 rate for a tenant), quick mitigations (temporary burst uplift, reduce client batch/concurrency, enable backoff), root cause probes (trace request ids, check model mix, check shard queue lengths), long-term fixes (better tenant-specific adaptive throttling, client SDK backoff helpers).

Marco (infra): Follow-ups: We'll also instrument per-tenant burst refill rates in the console for easier visibility. File a ticket and I'll pick it up next sprint.

DataCorp-ML: Restarted — initial run shows successful batches and no 429s so far. Also fixed the model tag mismatch. Thanks for the quick uplift + guidance.

Ava (support): Great news. Marking this thread P2-resolved for now. We'll keep the burst uplift active for another 10 minutes before automatic rollback. Please confirm if any residual errors.

DataCorp-ML: All clear. No more 429s, no dimension errors. Succeeded end-to-end. We'll notify if anything else. Thanks team! :tada:

Jin (eng-runtime): Adding final notes to the new runbook draft and recommended client changes. Action items: 
- Support create playbook doc (Ava)
- Runtime add SDK snippet for jittered backoff (Jin)
- Infra expose tenant burst metrics in Console (Marco)
- ML-support provide vector-dim sanity checks snippet (Priya)

Ava (support): Closing here; will attach the playbook once PR'd. Thread closed in 1h if no reopen.
